name: Pentapeptide-3
lead: Pentapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide name that is ambiguous in the literature. Before 2006, the INCI name palmitoyl pentapeptide-3 referred to the Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser (KTTKS) peptide sold as Matrixyl, since renamed palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 [1][2]. the available alias for this entry, Vialox, is separately marketed as a muscle-relaxing 'Botox-like' ingredient, and no loaded source describes it.

Available research on the KTTKS peptide family shows effects on collagen and extracellular-matrix production in cultured cells, and a 2019 study of 32 KTTKS analogues found none cytotoxic to fibroblasts [2]. No clinical study of a product specified as Vialox was found.
infobox: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-3 is the pre-2006 INCI name for KTTKS (now pentapeptide-4) [1][2]

paras: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl) is KTTKS joined to a 16-carbon palmitoyl chain, launched by Sederma around 2000 [1]. It is a matrikine, a peptide fragment thought to signal cells to produce extracellular matrix, and a 2019 paper notes it was previously labelled palmitoyl pentapeptide-3 [2].

No studies found for a product specified as pentapeptide-3 or Vialox. Studies of the related KTTKS peptide are mostly in vitro; the 2019 study found palmitoylated analogues inhibited serine proteases such as plasmin and thrombin in the laboratory and did not reproduce a previously reported 150 percent collagen increase [2].

timeline.event: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-3 is renamed palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 [2].

card.summary: An ambiguous peptide name: historically KTTKS (Matrixyl), also tied to Vialox; little verified evidence.
card.note: The name referred to different peptides at different times; check the full ingredient name.

quick.overview:
Pentapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide label whose meaning has changed: before 2006 it denoted palmitoyl KTTKS (Matrixyl), and it is also tied to the Vialox brand.

Research is mostly laboratory work on KTTKS-type peptides, and no clinical trial specific to Vialox was found.
quick.mechanism: KTTKS-type peptides are described as matrikines that signal cells to make collagen and other matrix proteins; Vialox is described by suppliers as reducing muscle signalling, which this wiki could not verify.
quick.risks: No adverse events were reported in the sources. A cell study found KTTKS analogues non-cytotoxic to fibroblasts.
